references.text: The prohibition against disgracing one's daughter through prostitution is linked to the ban on cultic prostitution in Israel.
During Rehoboam's reign, there were temple prostitutes in the land, showing how this commandment was broken in Israel's history.
King Asa removed the temple prostitutes from the land as part of his religious reform, in accordance with this prohibition.
Jehoshaphat removed the remaining temple prostitutes who had persisted since his father's time, in obedience to this command.
King Josiah tore down the houses of the temple prostitutes that were in the house of the Lord, as part of his great reform.
Hosea condemns cultic prostitution and shows how this prohibition remained relevant during the time of the prophets.
The story of Tamar uses the word 'kedesha' (temple prostitute), showing that this practice existed in Canaanite culture.
